newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain to put two alleged Qatari spies on trial.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain to put two alleged Qatari spies on trial.

text.p: Two Qataris arrested this week in Bahrain on charges of spying will be put on trial on Wednesday, a newspaper reported.
Al-Ayam newspaper, quoting an interior ministry source, said the two suspects -- a man and woman -- would face charges of providing intelligence to a foreign country and disclosing defence secrets.

Bahrain said on Monday the Qataris had confessed before an investigating judge to spying for Doha. They were named as Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri. The paper said relatives of the suspects had arrived in Manama and would attend the trial. Qatar denied they were spies.
The incident has raised tensions between Qatar and Bahrain, already locked in a territorial dispute over a group of barren islands, reefs and sandbanks controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.
Bahrain has said it will boycott this week's Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in the Qatari capital Doha, saying Qatar has behaved in an "unfriendly" manner.

Doha newspapers have said the spying charges were intended to undermine the summit and abort an initiative by Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani to visit Bahrain to try to persuade it not to boycott the summit.
